answer: We define a mechanism where dynamic opportunity-cost bonds coupled with subgame-perfect slashing matrices induce a negative expected value for Sybil identities. Each virtual pulse of the protocol updates the bond requirement, ensuring the cost to maintain a relic of multiple nodes exceeds any marginal gain. In this vast ocean of adversarial agents, we prove that truth-telling converges to a strict Nash equilibrium as costs scale superlinearly with identity count.
